candidates.name: Wenzel Circular Walk
candidates.reason: Pass B's find of the official route page names and sources what Pass A had already folded into the Chemin de la Corniche card as 'the spine of the Wenzel Circular Walk' — corroboration, not a new guide edit.

candidates.name: Vianden Castle
candidates.reason: Kept as the trip's one half-day-out: fortifications/history is the intake's #1 ranked priority (the traveler's comments explicitly name 'the old fortifications'), and the castle already carries complete T0-verified transport (R3 depth, corrected line-181 route) and reservation research. Pass B independently proposed Echternach/Mullerthal instead, partly reasoning from the stale 'bus 570' Ettelbrück connection Pass A's own research had already disproven (see dis-vianden-bus-line) — so Pass B's transfer-difficulty concern overstated the actual friction. Mullerthal/Echternach is retained as a genuine, well-sourced alternative (c-mullerthal-trail--echternach-loop, status: detour) rather than dropped — see dis-vianden-vs-mullerthal-halfday and ledger q-luxembourg-1.

candidates.name: Pfaffenthal Panoramic Elevator
candidates.reason: Independently corroborated by Pass B from a second official domain (visitluxembourg.com) with identical hours and free-of-charge fact.

candidates.name: Vianden Chairlift
candidates.reason: Couldn't confirm current price against a fetched official source within budget — search-only figures conflicted (€6.50 one-way vs €9 vs €16/couple). Left out of the shipped day plan rather than ship an unconfirmed figure.

candidates.name: Echternach & Müllerthal
candidates.reason: A real alternative half-day/day trip (hiking region + Roman abbey town), but the traveler wants at most one worthwhile trip out and Vianden Castle scores higher on the trip's top-ranked culture/history priority — this is a hiking-first destination, less fortifications-specific. Pass B independently researched the same destination in more depth as c-mullerthal-trail--echternach-loop (retained as a detour candidate).

candidates.name: Mullerthal Trail
candidates.reason: Pass B's independently researched half-day alternative to Vianden Castle: a direct, low-risk (R1) free bus (line 201, no transfer) to Echternach, with the Schiessentumpel waterfall loop corroborated quiet at opening by two independent firsthand French-language sources. Serves the trip's thinnest priority (nature/outdoors) better than another castle would. Not built into the day plan — Vianden Castle was kept as the trip's one half-day-out given its #1-priority alignment and already-complete depth research — but retained and noted on the Vianden Castle sights card plus flagged to the traveler (ledger q-luxembourg-1) as a swap option.

candidates.name: Schengen
candidates.reason: The Moselle tripoint viewpoint is more a symbolic photo stop than a culture/history or nature depth destination, and is further from the city than Vianden with a weaker transit connection.

candidates.name: Am Tiirmschen
candidates.reason: Permanently closed — the restaurant stopped serving customers end of October 2023 and officially closed end of November 2023 per the operator's own account to local press. A frequent generic-guide recommendation that no longer exists.

candidates.name: Um Plateau
candidates.reason: Reservation-recommended/table-booking oriented per its own listings, which runs against the traveler's stated preference to eat well without booking anything formal.

candidates.name: Brasserie Guillaume
candidates.reason: Long all-day hours suggested walk-in viability, but the operator's own page carried no hours or booking-policy detail and a second official confirmation couldn't be reached within budget — omitted rather than ship an unconfirmed walk-in claim.

candidates.name: Um Dierfgen
candidates.reason: The guidebook-default address for Luxembourgish specialties in the capital. Multiple independent review sources (resto.lu, TripAdvisor listing text seen via search) consistently describe it as full and effectively needing a reservation at lunch and dinner — the opposite of the party's stated 'eat well without booking anything formal.' Could not fetch the operator's own site to confirm or refute directly (umdierfgen.lu returned 403 on both a direct attempt and a mirror retry), so no reservation-policy evidence record ships for it — but the weight of consistent secondary reports is enough to route the recommendation elsewhere.

candidates.name: Manzoku Ramen Bar
candidates.reason: Genuinely walk-in-only by design (no reservation system exists at all, virtual queue instead), matching the party's preference exactly. Only open Wed–Sat, so only Friday and Saturday of this Fri–Mon stay fall inside its hours. Added to the guide's Food & shopping list with its exact street address flagged as not independently confirmed this pass (Pass B's evidence gave hours/policy but no address).

candidates.name: Kaito Ramen
candidates.reason: Walk-in/first-come-first-served daily (Place de Paris location), open every day of the Oct 16–19 stay, which Manzoku is not. Corroborated as genuinely busy at midday by two independent sources, so best used as a just-before-noon or dinner pick.

candidates.name: Konrad Cafe & Bar
candidates.reason: Repeatedly mentioned as a casual, walk-in-friendly local favourite (well-known carrot cake). Only one directly-fetched firsthand source found within budget (planethibbel.com); a second independent firsthand source was not secured (a second candidate article truncated on fetch). Held as a lead, not shipped as a corroborated experiential pick.

candidates.name: Beim Siggy
candidates.reason: Clausen brasserie repeatedly recommended for Luxembourgish food with a valley view over the Grund. Could not corroborate firsthand within the two-attempt fetch budget: the one personal-blog write-up found no longer resolves (DNS failure), and TripAdvisor returned 403 on every attempt this pass (restaurant review page, forum thread, and a mirror retry). Omitted rather than shipped unverified.

candidates.name: Chiggeri
candidates.reason: Well-regarded but consistently positioned and reviewed as upscale fine dining with an extensive wine list — the wrong register for 'eat well without booking anything formal.' Not pursued further.

evidence.claim: A US passport holder may enter Luxembourg visa-free for stays up to 90 days within any 180-day period (Schengen short-stay rule); ETIAS pre-authorization for visa-exempt travelers is expected to apply from late 2026.
Public transport (bus, tram, 2nd-class rail) has been free nationwide since 1 March 2020; 1st-class rail and cross-border tickets remain paid, and free fare ends at the border.
Bus lines 16 and 29 connect Findel Airport to the city centre/central station every 10–15 minutes, free of charge within Luxembourg; the tram also serves the airport.
Airport taxi pickup has moved to Kiss & Fly Parking C during ongoing tram construction.
Bock Casemates open daily, every 15 min from 09:45 to 19:00 (last admission), closed Dec 25 & Jan 1; adult admission €11.

Luxembourg City's Old Quarters and Fortifications were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List on 17 December 1994, recognizing the fortress complex spanning the 16th–19th centuries before its 1867 partial demolition.

The Chemin de la Corniche, called "the most beautiful balcony of Europe" by writer Batty Weber, runs along the 17th-century ramparts from the Bock promontory to the Holy Ghost Citadel; it is free, open-air, and forms the spine of the Wenzel Circular Walk.

Nationalmusée um Fëschmaart (MNHA) open Tue–Wed & Fri–Sun 10:00–18:00, Thu 10:00–20:00, closed Mondays; individual admission €7, combined ticket with Musée Dräi Eechelen €12, free for under-26s and the last hour before closing.
Musée Dräi Eechelen open Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 (Wed to 20:00), closed Mondays; individual admission €7, combined same-day ticket with MNHA €12, group rate (6+) €5.
Villa Vauban open Mon, Wed, Thu, Sat & Sun 10:00–18:00, Fri 10:00–21:00, closed Tuesdays and Nov 1/Dec 25/Jan 1; adult admission €5, free every Friday 18:00–21:00.
Notre-Dame Cathedral is free to enter, open daily 08:00–18:00 (to 19:00 Sundays), except during services.

Grand Ducal Palace interior guided tours (75 min, sold by the Luxembourg City Tourist Office) run 18 July–30 August 2026 only; the changing of the guard in 2026 falls on 22 June, 18 July, and 5 September, all at 16:00 — none inside an October visit window.

The Pfaffenthal panoramic elevator runs daily 05:45–01:00, free of charge, connecting Pescatore park (upper town) to Pfaffenthal (Alzette valley floor); closed for maintenance the first Monday of each month from 09:00 to 05:45 the next day.
The Pfaffenthal panoramic elevator is completely free to use.

The Grund is a former tanners'/millers' quarter set deep in the Alzette valley, part of the 1994 UNESCO fortifications listing, with cobbled lanes (some dating to the 10th century) along the riverfront.

Neumünster Abbey (neimënster) cultural centre in the Grund is open daily 10:00–18:00; its cloister and courtyard are free to visit, with a paid guided-tour option and the Wenzel route running through it.

The Pétrusse Valley is a free public park along the old fortress moat below the old town, with walking/jogging trails and a fitness park at Rue d'Anvers, reached from the city centre via stone staircases.

Vianden Castle, October hours: daily 10:00–17:00, last entry 16:30 (seasonal ranges apply other months); adult admission €13 (incl. €1 municipal tourist tax), student (13+) €7, child (6–12) €4; closed Jan 1, Nov 2, Dec 25.

The current public-transport connection to Vianden is CFL train to Ettelbrück + RGTR bus line 181 (Ettelbrück – Vianden – Obereisenbach); the Ettelbrück mobility hub was reorganized starting 10 May 2026, with several lines' stops relocated, and the current line 181 timetable is valid as of that date — which covers this trip's October 2026 dates.

From 10 May 2026 the Ettelbrück mobility hub's bus station was completely reorganized with new bus stops brought into service, as part of ongoing hub construction — the official notice does not itself name which lines are affected, but the line 181 timetable (see ev-vianden-route-line-181) is separately stamped valid from the same date.

The Place Guillaume II market runs Wednesdays and Saturdays, 07:30–14:00 (city page states 07:30–14:00; a food-stall cluster within it ran 10:30–14:00 through Oct 2024 per the same page), with regional produce, cheese, roast chicken and artisanal goods.

Mousel's Cantine (46 Montée de Clausen), open Mon–Sat 11:45–14:00 & 18:00–22:00, Sun 12:00–16:00; appetizers €9–28, mains €24–69, desserts €9–11; the site offers online booking and encourages reservations, walk-in availability not explicitly stated.

Mousel's Cantine has operated in the same Clausen building for 200 years, serving traditional Luxembourgish dishes including Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked pork collar with broad beans), the country's national dish.
Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked/cured pork collar with broad beans, boiled potatoes) is considered Luxembourg's national dish, associated with the village of Gostingen.
Oberweis has operated since 1964, moved to the Grand-Rue flagship location in 1970 with a first-floor tearoom, and has been supplier to the Grand Ducal court since 1999.

Um Plateau's own listing prompts "Réserver une table" (reserve a table) as its primary call to action, linking to its own booking system — indicating a reservation-oriented service model, though the page doesn't explicitly state whether reservations are required or merely recommended.
112 is the nationwide emergency number. A rotating duty pharmacy (pharmacie de garde) keeps at least one pharmacy open 24 hours (8am–8am), listed at pharmacie.lu and posted in every pharmacy window.
Luxembourg has no legally mandated restaurant service charge; tipping is optional, and rounding up or adding 5–10% for standout service is the common practice.
Luxembourg has three official languages (Luxembourgish, French, German); French is dominant in shops/signage, and roughly 80% of the population also speaks English.

A brief handshake is the standard Luxembourg greeting even in casual encounters; cheek-kissing is reserved for people who already know each other and never happens between two men; social register is reserved/formal until a relationship is established.

Luxembourg in October averages 13°C/6°C day/night, with roughly 70–87mm of rain spread across 11–15 days of the month — moderate, not a distinct monsoon-style rainy season, but frequent enough to warrant an indoor fallback for outdoor days.

Luxembourg observes 11 nationwide public holidays in 2026 (New Year's, Easter Monday, Labour Day, Europe Day, Ascension, Whit Monday, National Day, Assumption, All Saints', Christmas, Boxing Day) — none fall inside this trip's Oct 16–19 window; the closest is All Saints' Day (Nov 1).

The Wenzel Circular Walk is a free, self-guided ~2.5km/3-hour signposted route (named for Duke Wenceslas II) that links the Bock rock/casemates, the medieval Wenzel-era fortifications, the Chemin de la Corniche and the upper and lower town — a single route through the exact combination of fortifications and valley-adjacent walking this party asked for.
Bock Casemates: open daily (year-round except Dec 25 and Jan 1), entry every 15 minutes from 09:45 to 19:00 (last admission), maximum 45 minutes per visit; adult admission EUR11.00 (2026).

The Pfaffenthal Panoramic Elevator is free, rises 71m connecting Pescatore Park in the upper town to the Pfaffenthal district at the bottom of the Alzette valley, and runs daily 05:45-01:00 (closed for maintenance the first Monday of each month, 09:00 to 05:45 the next day) -- a practical way to walk down into the valley and ride back up rather than reclimbing.

Public transport (bus, tram, and 2nd-class train) has been free throughout the entire territory of Luxembourg since 1 March 2020, for residents and visitors alike; only 1st-class rail travel requires a paid ticket.
RGTR bus line 201 runs Luxembourg City (Limpertsberg) - Echternach directly, no transfer, free like all Luxembourg public transport.

Schiessentumpel is the busiest point on the Mullerthal Trail loop near Echternach; walking it right at opening, before the day's tour/hiking groups arrive, changes the experience -- noticeably quieter and near-empty at the falls.

Schiessentumpel is the busiest point on the Mullerthal Trail loop near Echternach; walking it right at opening, before the day's tour/hiking groups arrive, changes the experience -- noticeably quieter and near-empty at the falls.

Manzoku Ramen Bar takes no reservations at all (virtual waitlist queue via an app once full); open only Wednesday-Saturday (Wed-Thu 11:30-14:00, Fri 11:30-14:00 and 18:00-21:00, Sat 18:00-22:00), closed Sunday-Tuesday.
Kaito (Place de Paris location) is walk-in / first-come-first-served daily 11:30-21:30; only groups of 8 or more can book a table in advance.

Kaito's Place de Paris location gets genuinely busy at midday; since it's walk-in only (no reservations except groups of 8+), arriving by or around noon on a weekday is the practical way to get a table without a long wait.

Kaito's Place de Paris location gets genuinely busy at midday; since it's walk-in only (no reservations except groups of 8+), arriving by or around noon on a weekday is the practical way to get a table without a long wait.

Luxembourg has three official languages (Luxembourgish, French, German). French is the most consistently useful single language for visitors in shops, cafes and restaurants, especially in the capital; roughly 80% of the population also speaks English as a practical backup. Locals themselves switch between all three day to day: Luxembourgish for broadcast media and everyday talk, German for print, French for business and formal matters.

reservations.foreignFriction: Phone booking (+352 27 67 23 42) or the site's own form; no evidence of a foreign-card or foreign-phone barrier.
reservations.walkIn: Lunch generally seats walk-ins per the operator's own site; dinner is not confirmed walk-in-friendly and the site itself encourages booking — this directly bears on the traveler's stated preference to avoid formal booking, so it's flagged rather than assumed.

leads.claim: Weekend dinner (Fri–Sat) is the highest-risk seating for a walk-in to fail.

reservations.alternatives: The Wed/Sat Place Guillaume II market, Oberweis, and the two walk-in-only ramen spots (Kaito Ramen daily, Manzoku Ramen Bar Wed–Sat) all need no booking at any time and can absorb a dinner that doesn't work out at Mousel's.
reservations.fallback: Arrive for lunch instead (11:45 seating), which the operator's own page treats as normal walk-in service.

reservations.walkIn: Walk-up ticketing at the castle gate; the official site describes no online-booking requirement for individual visitors (only group tours contact the administration by email).
reservations.fallback: If the bus 181 connection runs late or is missed, the next departure per the reorganized Ettelbrück hub schedule should still allow a same-day visit given the castle's 10:00–17:00 October hours — confirm via the mobiliteit.lu app rather than assuming a fixed interval.

transport.route: Luxembourg City → Ettelbrück (CFL train) → Vianden (RGTR bus 181)
transport.doorToDoor: ≈50–70 min each way (train to Ettelbrück + bus 181 connection), both legs free nationwide transit.
transport.transferReality: Cross-platform-adjacent at Ettelbrück per aggregator descriptions, but the whole hub was physically reorganized 10 May 2026 (new platforms, some stops relocated) — the pre-reorg mental model of the transfer no longer applies.
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Not a factor for this day trip — no luggage carried, two able walkers.
transport.buffer: Build 15–20 min slack at Ettelbrück given the hub reorganization; don't plan a tight back-to-back connection on the outbound leg.
transport.missedConnection: RGTR routes in this corridor have historically run roughly half-hourly to hourly; a missed connection costs time, not the day, given the castle's wide October opening window (10:00–17:00).
transport.nextService: Not independently confirmed post-reorganization — check the mobiliteit.lu app or call the Mobilitéitszentral (+352 2465 2465) the morning of.
transport.lastPracticalReturn: Plan to leave Vianden by mid-to-late afternoon; the castle's last entry is 16:30 in October and free nationwide transit stays available through the evening on the same route.
transport.fallback: A taxi from Vianden back to Ettelbrück or direct to Luxembourg City is a fallback if the bus connection fails outright — not priced or booked in advance for this trip.

transport.route: Luxembourg City (Limpertsberg) to Echternach via RGTR bus line 201
transport.doorToDoor: Direct bus, no transfer, free of charge; runs roughly every 30 minutes per aggregator schedules (not independently fetched from the official timetable PDF this pass).
transport.groupLuggageMobility: Not relevant for a 2-person half-day trip with no luggage.
transport.nextService: Every ~30 minutes through the day (per mobiliteit.lu line page and third-party timetable aggregators).
transport.fallback: Lines 211/212 also connect Luxembourg City to Echternach via a longer routing through intermediate villages, per the Mullerthal Trail's own mobility page (not independently fetched by Pass B).

disagreements.topic: Whether MNHA (Nationalmusée um Fëschmaart) permanent-exhibition admission is free or a paid €7.
disagreements.investigation: An initial search-engine summary claimed permanent exhibitions are free; fetching the museum's own official practical-info page directly showed a standard €7 individual ticket (free only for under-26s, the last hour before close, and Thursday 17:30–20:00).
disagreements.resolution: Resolved in favor of the fetched official source (nationalmusee.lu): €7 individual, with the specific free windows/categories listed above. The guide ships the official figure.

disagreements.topic: Which bus line connects Ettelbrück to Vianden — older aggregator sources cite "bus 570," the official transit authority lists line 181.
disagreements.investigation: Multiple travel-forum/aggregator sources named bus 570. Searching the official mobiliteit.lu line directory found no line 570 serving this corridor, but found line 181 (Ettelbrück–Vianden–Obereisenbach) with an official PDF timetable stamped valid from 10 May 2026, alongside an official notice that the Ettelbrück hub was reorganized on that date.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved in favor of the official, current source: line 181, not 570 — the aggregator figure appears to be stale pre-reorganization information. The guide and a 'What generic guides get wrong' entry both carry the corrected line number, with a flag to reconfirm the live departure time given how recently the hub changed.

disagreements.topic: Whether Luxembourg restaurants add a legally mandated 15% service charge (as in France/Belgium) or tipping is fully optional.
disagreements.investigation: One aggregator-style search result claimed a 15% service charge is added and included. A directly fetched Luxembourg-focused publication (luxtoday.lu) states explicitly that, unlike France and Belgium, Luxembourg does not require a service charge by law, and tipping (5–10%, or rounding up) is optional custom.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved in favor of the fetched, Luxembourg-specific source. The guide states tipping as optional/customary, not a mandated charge.

disagreements.topic: Bock Casemates opening hours and adult admission price
disagreements.investigation: Initial aggregator/search results gave 10:00-17:00 (18:00 in summer), open March 1-November 2 only, adult price cited as either EUR8 or EUR4. Fetching the operator's own current page (luxembourg-city.com) directly showed a different picture: open year-round except Dec 25/Jan 1, timed entries every 15 minutes from 09:45-19:00, adult EUR11.00 (2026).
disagreements.resolution: Treated the fetched operator page as the current T0 source over the older/lower secondary figures; see ev-casemates-hours-price. Does not change any recommendation, only the specific hours/price to publish. Independently corroborates Pass A's own ev-bock-casemates-hours-price.

disagreements.topic: Which single half-day trip out of the city to build into the plan — Vianden Castle (fortifications/history) or the Mullerthal Trail/Echternach loop (nature/hiking) — since the traveler asked for at most one.
disagreements.investigation: Pass A researched and fully depth-verified Vianden Castle (T0 hours/price, R3 transport route via Ettelbrück + bus 181, reservation-friction check) as the half-day trip, given the trip's #1 ranked priority is culture/history and the intake specifically names 'the old fortifications.' Pass B, working independently toward the trip's thinnest priority (nature/outdoors), proposed Echternach/Mullerthal instead — a direct, low-risk (R1) bus with no transfer, and corroborated (two independent firsthand French-language sources) that visiting the Schiessentumpel waterfall right at opening avoids the day's crowds. Pass B's stated case against Vianden partly relied on the same stale 'bus 570' Ettelbrück connection that Pass A's own research had already disproven in favor of the current line 181 (see dis-vianden-bus-line) — so Pass B underestimated how solid Vianden's actual transfer now is.
disagreements.resolution: Kept Vianden Castle as the built half-day trip: it directly serves the trip's top-ranked priority (with the traveler's comments explicitly naming 'the old fortifications'), and its transport/reservation depth research is already complete and current. Mullerthal/Echternach is retained as a genuine, well-sourced alternative (c-mullerthal-trail--echternach-loop, status: detour) — noted on the Vianden Castle sights card and flagged to the traveler via ledger question q-luxembourg-1 as a swap option for a more hiking-focused day.

saturation.note: Both passes independently reached saturation on the same core clusters (upper-town fortifications/museums, the Grund/valley walk, and Luxembourg City dining), converging on matching hours/prices for every venue both researched. Pass B's native French/German sweep surfaced two significant net-new finds Pass A's English-first pass missed — the Wenzel Circular Walk's official page, and two firsthand-corroborated walk-in ramen picks (Kaito Ramen, Manzoku Ramen Bar) that fit the traveler's no-formal-booking preference better than anything Pass A shipped — both adopted into the guide at reconcile. The one live disagreement requiring judgment (Vianden Castle vs. Mullerthal/Echternach as the trip's one half-day-out) was resolved in favor of Vianden given its priority-#1 alignment and already-complete transport/reservation depth, with Mullerthal retained as a flagged alternative rather than dropped. Remaining unresolved items (Vianden chairlift pricing, Konrad Cafe & Bar's second corroborating source, Am Tiirmschen/Um Dierfgen/Beim Siggy's blocked confirmations, Manzoku's exact street address) are minor and would not change any shipped recommendation.

nativeLanguage.why: Luxembourg's genuine resident-angle content (personal travel blogs, culinary press, forum-style reviews) runs mostly in French and German rather than English tourist coverage; Luxembourgish itself is rarely used for this kind of written web content, so 'native-first' here meant leaning on French/German queries rather than literal Luxembourgish translations, plus a French/German-domain filter over the usual English top-10.
